questions.q: What four elements make up purposeful practice?
a: A specific goal, focus, pushing past comfort and feedback
Talent, money, free time and good luck
A mentor, a textbook, a schedule and rest
Motivation, competition, rewards and praise
questions.why: Lesson 1 lists a clear goal, focus, constant pushing and feedback as the four parts of purposeful practice.

questions.q: How many digits could Steve remember after months of training?
a: 82 digits
12 digits
40 digits
100 digits
questions.why: Lesson 1 describes Steve going from seven digits to sequences of up to 82.

questions.q: What two things turn purposeful practice into deliberate practice?
a: A well-established field and a guiding mentor
Longer sessions and much harder goals
Public competition and cash prizes
Natural talent and an early start
questions.why: Lesson 2 says purposeful practice becomes deliberate in a mature field with a coach or mentor.

questions.q: What does Ericsson say about Mozart's talent?
a: He received intensive training from his father early on
He was born with an unusual musical gift
He composed masterpieces as a toddler
He had no formal training at all
questions.why: Lesson 3 says Mozart received excellent training from his father before he was four.

questions.q: What does the summary say about starting points in performance?
a: Whoever practices the most deliberately wins out
Starting talent decides the final outcome
Only children can become truly world-class
Practice matters less than natural genetics
questions.why: Lesson 3 concludes that whoever practices the most deliberately wins, whatever the starting point.
